summary.headline: Denta FY26 revenue rose over 23% to Rs 2,503.8 mn with order book of Rs 7,278 mn, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and management gave no firm order-inflow guidance.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,503.8 mn (over 23% growth), EBITDA of Rs 834.9 mn and PAT of Rs 609 mn, with an order book of about Rs 7,278 mn across 38 ongoing projects as of March 31, 2026. Analysts pressed on a sharp Q3/Q4 run-rate slowdown and a Q4 EBITDA margin of about 19% versus roughly 33% in the first three quarters, which management attributed to the Iran-US war, petroleum-linked raw material costs and a mix shift to smaller projects. Order-book inflow was described as pending new tenders under the new Karnataka government, with no order value committed. Working capital of about Rs 295 crore (inventory, receivables and other assets) is expected to convert largely in December-January, and management guided to about 20% FY27 revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of around 25%.

segments.name: Water management (core)
segments.commentary: Management says about 90% of the water order book sits in the water sector, covering drinking water, STP, irrigation and tank regeneration. The company has bagged 3-4 FTP projects covering about 15-16 cities in Karnataka.

segments.name: Amrut 2 and Jal Jivan Mission
segments.commentary: One Amrut 2 order of Rs 232 crore (Kuknuru and Yelburga, Koppal) and four Jal Jivan Mission projects in Karnataka. Management says about 70% of these projects is complete, with the balance 30% targeted this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% stated as the minimum projection; closing remarks cited a 20-25% target.
EBITDA margin guided at about 25% (confirmed in Q&A), down from about 33% run-rate in Q1-Q3 FY26.
No firm order-inflow number given; management expects to announce new orders shortly and aims for a healthy order-book increase by end-March 2027.
Management declined to give an absolute FY27 profit figure, saying it depends on project execution and raw material investment.
Government payments expected to accelerate from July-August 2026, with many payments in Q2-Q3 FY27, per management.
Possible price-escalation relief for HDPE/PVC items expected in July or Q2 FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Inventory, receivables and other assets of about Rs 295 crore are tied up in working capital; management expects about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) to be realised in FY27, mainly by December-January.
Payment on supply is roughly 55% after material is laid, with the balance 35% on laying and the remainder on completion, per management.
Company is adopting NEBR and CAMUS-based STP technologies, claiming about 95% purity, largely through subcontracting to patent holders.
Bidding pipeline of about 5-6 projects worth about Rs 600 crore; management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and 2-3 major tenders.
Four to five projects identified in Madhya Pradesh under the National Water Management Programme (NWMP); a Mahanadi barrage tender in Odisha is yet to be floated.
demand_pricing: Karnataka's new government (formed late May/early June 2026) is expected to push infrastructure tenders after a roughly six-month slowdown.
Raw material risk: 20-30% of raw material is UPVC and HDPE pipe, with prices up in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026 after the Iran-US war; some suppliers seeking higher prices.
Price escalation clauses exist on projects above Rs 100 crore but not on smaller projects, per management.
Management said the company is taking smaller-value projects (Rs 10-50 crore) alongside larger ones (up to Rs 300 crore), which dilutes margin.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 execution slowdown was attributed to war-related disruption and irregular payments.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of order flow and government payment status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders in the coming quarter; payments are expected to pick up from July-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said margin would be maintained around 30%, then confirmed a 25% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 after repeated questioning; it said smaller projects will dilute margin.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital liquidation timeline (Rs 295 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects cash in December-January, with about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) targeted in FY27, after laying and completion of projects by October.

qa_highlights.question: Order book fall from Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the reduction to revenue conversion and investment in completing old projects, and said the audit team would provide the exact reconciliation; it did not confirm any cancellation.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a minimum of 20% revenue growth but declined to give an absolute profit number, saying it depends on project implementation and raw material investment.

qa_highlights.question: Diversification beyond Karnataka and into private industrial segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NWMP projects in Madhya Pradesh and a biogas project with a partner holding GAIL and BPCL contracts; no firm private industrial wins were disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin about 19% versus about 33% in Q1-Q3; FY27 guidance of 25% implies lower profit growth against a 20% revenue rise.
Working-capital conversion: about Rs 295 crore in inventory, receivables and other assets; collection timing rests on government payments.
Order book fell from about Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026), with no reconciliation provided on the call.
Government dependence and political transition in Karnataka; payment timing is uncertain.
Raw material inflation from petroleum-linked pipes (UPVC and HDPE), with suppliers seeking higher prices.
Management answers on key numbers were vague or deferred to later written follow-up, including order-book reconciliation, margin split by project size and profit guidance.
summary.management_tone: Management was upbeat and forward-looking on the new government's infrastructure push and order prospects, but evasive on specifics: it deferred the order-book reconciliation, margin split, and absolute profit figures to a later written follow-up. Its margin and payment answers shifted between statements, and it only confirmed the 25% EBITDA guidance after repeated questioning.

growth.why: Management guides about 20% FY27 revenue growth as a minimum, backed by the Rs 7,278 mn order book across 38 projects, but no firm new-order number was given, Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and the EBITDA margin guide of 25-30% is not firm.
